title: 4 Logo elasticity
slide_intent: Pair movement with its behavior curve so a designer can relate a visible response to an underlying timing model.
strategic_value: A repeatable elastic response can make Channel 4’s logo feel active without arbitrary movement.
demonstration: The video pairs the green 4 with a curve that rises and falls as the mark shifts; the published poster uses a different S-shaped curve.
practical_value: Compare the displayed motion with the accompanying curve instead of copying a single still as a complete easing specification.

content_islands.name: Logo specimen
content_islands.spec: Place the green 4 on a black stage at left.

content_islands.name: Curve specimen
content_islands.spec: Place the animated curve and moving highlight at right under the elasticity heading.

reference_purposes.Application: The film pairs a moving logo with a behavior-curve demonstration.
reference_purposes.Intent: Pentagram attributes the logo’s reactive dynamism to physics-based elasticity.

ingredient.name: Logo elasticity
ingredient.role: Give the identity a responsive physical character.
ingredient.application: Use the paired animation and curve to understand the demonstrated response.
ingredient.scope: The video and published poster show different curves; this record does not infer a universal numeric easing value.
